question.value: Physical properties and cold gas content of 16 Hot DOGs at z ∼ 3; their role in massive galaxy and SMBH coevolution.

evidence.quote: To investigate systematically the physical properties of Hot DOGs at z $\sim$ 3, particularly their cold gas content, we conduct a comprehensive UV to millimeter SED analysis of a subsample of 16 Hot DOGs selected from (cite: Fan2016b).
Most of our sample sources were observed in our project 2017.1.00441.S (PI: L. Fan).
A few sources were allocated to a different project and available in the ALMA archive (2017.1.00358.S), and we also include these observations.
Observations were carried out with ALMA using the Band-3 and Band-4 receivers during Cycle 5.

referee_caveats_inferred: Gas depletion and AGN feedback are inferred from population comparisons and correlations; these analyses do not establish feedback causality.
Fixed CO excitation ratios and αCO introduce systematic uncertainty beyond individual line-flux errors.
The 30–50 K dust-temperature restriction materially changes LIR, SFR, SFE, and dust-derived quantities.
Table 1 optical redshifts differ from later CO redshifts; reproduction must specify which redshift enters each calculation.
The prose names W0149+2305, whereas the sample tables name W0149+2350.
The SFE units printed in the paper are inconsistent with the stated LIR/L′CO definition; retain the printed units when checking answer keys.
Table 7 and the conclusion disagree on the lower uncertainty of MBH/Mstar: 0.021 versus 0.026.
Tentative detections are tabulated as Gaussian measurements while prose also discusses four nondetections; sample-statistic treatment needs clarification.
The reported Bayes factor is described as a difference in Bayesian evidence; its exact numerical convention needs clarification.
Black hole masses and growth rates depend directly on fixed λEdd and η/(1−η), rather than independent mass measurements for the full sample.
